key_insight: A bismuth density functional tight binding model with explicit spin–orbit coupling maps topology-related electronic changes at approximately 1,000 times the computational efficiency of DFT.
engineering_relevance: The model enables large-scale screening of how strain and buckling affect bismuthene’s electronic structure and topological classification.
method: Develop a transferable bismuth DFTB model with explicit spin–orbit coupling.
Screen bismuthene structures to map band gap closure and band inversion versus strain and buckling.
Validate electronic, structural, vibrational, and topological predictions against DFT.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports accurate rhombohedral band structures, transferability tests on phonons and additional solid phases, and DFT comparisons of optimized bilayers, band inversion, and the Z₂ invariant.
watch_item: Validation is specific to the tested bismuth structures; accuracy for other materials or unexplored structural regimes remains unestablished.
paper_title: A Density Functional Tight Binding Model for Rapid Screening of Spin-Orbit-Coupling-Driven Topological Properties in Bismuth
